items.title: Numerical reasoning: compound change, reverse percentages and profit (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: The hardest percentage questions combine several ideas, so plan the steps before you calculate. To remove VAT from a price that includes 20%, divide by 1.2, because the price is 120% of the original. A price of £150 including VAT was £125 before VAT. Repeated percentage falls, such as a machine losing 10% of its value each year, are repeated multipliers: £20,000 × 0.9 × 0.9 = £16,200. A fall followed by a rise needs both multipliers: 80,000 falling to 72,000 and then rising 25% gives 72,000 × 1.25 = 90,000. Profit on cost is the percentage added to the cost: a 35% profit on £60 gives 60 × 1.35 = £81. Percentage points and percentages differ. Approval rising from 40% to 50% is a rise of 10 percentage points, but a 25% increase, because 10 ÷ 40 = 0.25. Several changes in a row can almost cancel: a rise of 10%, another 10% and a fall of 20% gives 1.1 × 1.1 × 0.8 = 0.968, which is a 3.2% fall. If a reduced price is known, divide by the multiplier to find the original: £84 after a 30% reduction was £84 ÷ 0.7 = £120. Always ask whether the percentage applies to the original or the new figure.

questions.prompt: A price including 20% VAT is £150. What was the price before VAT was added?
A machine bought for £20,000 loses 10% of its current value each year. What is it worth after two years?
A town's population falls from 80,000 to 72,000 and then rises by 25%. What is the population after the rise?
A shop buys goods for £60 and adds a profit of 35% of the cost. What is the selling price?
Staff costs are 55% of a budget. Staff costs are then cut by 10%. What percentage of the original budget is now spent on staff?
Public approval of a service rises from 40% to 50%. By what percentage has approval increased?
questions.hint: The rise is 10 points; 10 ÷ 40 = 0.25, which is 25%.

questions.prompt: A value rises by 10%, rises by a further 10% and then falls by 20%. What is the overall change?

options.text: The value is unchanged
A fall of 3.2%
A fall of 0.1%
A rise of 3.2%

questions.hint: 1.1 × 1.1 × 0.8 = 0.968, so the value is 96.8% of the start.

questions.prompt: After a 30% reduction, an item costs £84. What was its original price?

items.title: Numerical reasoning: ratios, averages and proportion in several steps (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: These problems link ratios, averages and proportion, and they need a clear plan. If two people share money in the ratio 3:5 and the difference between the shares is £1,200, the difference is 2 parts, so one part is £600 and the total is 8 parts, £4,800. For averages, work with totals. Ten results with a mean of 62 give a total of 620. Removing 50 and 70 leaves 500 across 8 results, a mean of 62.5. When a ratio changes after people join, set up an equation with a letter for one part. If men and women are in the ratio 4:5 and 6 more men make it 1:1, then 4k + 6 = 5k, so k = 6 and there are 30 women. A weighted score applies a weight to each part: 40% coursework at 70 and 60% exam at 85 gives 0.4 × 70 + 0.6 × 85 = 79. Average speed over several legs is the total distance divided by the total time. Direct proportion keeps the rate steady: rate per person per day. Inverse proportion keeps the total work steady: 12 staff for 15 days is 180 staff-days, so 18 staff need 10 days. Check the final answer against the question.

questions.prompt: Profit is shared between two partners in the ratio 3:5. The second partner receives £1,200 more than the first. What was the total profit?
questions.hint: The difference is 2 parts = £1,200, so 1 part = £600; 8 parts = £4,800.

questions.prompt: Ten test results have a mean of 62. Two results, 50 and 70, are removed. What is the mean of the remaining eight?
The ratio of men to women in a team is 4:5. When 6 more men join, the numbers are equal. How many women are in the team?
questions.hint: 4k + 6 = 5k gives k = 6, so women = 5 × 6 = 30.

questions.prompt: A van travels at 40 mph for 2 hours and then at 60 mph for 3 hours. What is its average speed for the whole journey?

options.text: 52 mph
50 mph
48 mph
52.5 mph

questions.hint: Distance 80 + 180 = 260 miles; time 5 hours; 260 ÷ 5 = 52 mph.

questions.prompt: A course mark is 40% coursework and 60% exam. A candidate scores 70 in coursework and 85 in the exam. What is the overall mark?
Five staff process 400 applications in 8 days. At the same rate, how many days would 8 staff need for 600 applications?

options.text: 5 days
6 days
7.5 days
12 days

questions.hint: Rate is 10 applications per person per day; 600 ÷ 80 = 7.5 days.

questions.prompt: Twelve staff can finish a project in 15 days. How many days would 18 staff need, working at the same rate?

options.text: 22.5 days
8 days
12 days
10 days

questions.hint: Total work is 180 staff-days; 180 ÷ 18 = 10 days.

questions.prompt: Concentrate is mixed with water in the ratio 1:4. How much concentrate is needed for 2.5 litres of the mixed drink?

options.text: 500 ml
625 ml
50 ml

questions.hint: There are 5 parts, so 2.5 ÷ 5 = 0.5 litres, which is 500 ml.

items.title: Numerical reasoning: interest, pay and costing decisions (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Level 5 money questions ask you to make a decision from the numbers. Compound interest adds interest to the balance each year, so £5,000 at 4% for two years is £5,000 × 1.04 × 1.04 = £5,408, which is £8 more than simple interest. For a cost with a fixed part and a rate per unit, take away the fixed cost before you divide: with £400 fixed and £12 a unit, a £1,000 budget buys (1,000 − 400) ÷ 12 = 50 units. Pay questions often include more than one deduction. If gross pay is £2,800, tax of 20% applies only to pay above £1,000, so tax is £360, and 8% national insurance on the gross is £224, giving £2,216 net. When comparing suppliers, work out the full cost of each, including delivery and discounts, and then compare. Supplier A at £2.40 a unit for 500 units is £1,200. Supplier B at £2.20 plus £60 delivery is £1,160. Supplier C at £2.30 with 5% off is £1,092.50. Part-time leave is pro rata: 3 days out of 5 is 3/5 of 28 days. A currency exchange that returns less than you started with shows a loss caused by a worse rate on the way back. Be systematic and keep each stage on separate lines.

questions.prompt: £5,000 is saved at 4% compound interest a year. What is the balance after two years?
A project has fixed costs of £400 plus £12 for each unit made. The budget is £1,000. What is the largest number of units that can be made?
An employee's gross monthly pay is £2,800. Tax at 20% is paid on pay above £1,000 and national insurance at 8% on the gross pay. What is the net pay?
Maria changes £600 into euros at €1.20 to the pound. Later the rate is €1.25 to the pound and she changes all her euros back. How much less than £600 does she receive?
A supplier must be chosen. A charges £2.40 a unit for 500 units. B charges £2.20 a unit plus £60 delivery. C charges £2.30 a unit with 5% off the total. Which is cheapest for 500 units?

options.text: Supplier B, at £1,160
Supplier C, at £1,092.50
Supplier A, at £1,200
Supplier C, at £1,150

questions.prompt: Full-time annual leave is 28 days for a five-day week. How many days does a part-time worker on a three-day week receive, pro rata?

options.text: 11.2 days
9.33 days
84 days
16.8 days

questions.prompt: A mileage rate of 45p applies. Priya makes three trips, each 38 miles each way. What does she claim in total?
Rent of £850 is 34% of a household's monthly income. What is the monthly income?
questions.hint: Divide by the percentage: £850 ÷ 0.34 = £2,500.

items.title: Numerical reasoning: interpreting data and comparing groups (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Data questions at level 5 ask you to compare groups of different sizes, so raw numbers can mislead. To compare fairly, convert to a rate, share or percentage. Site A with 54 passes from 72 candidates has a pass rate of 75%, while Site B with 45 from 50 has 90%, so Site B is 15 percentage points higher even though Site A passed more people. For surpluses, compare the surplus as a share of income. A year with a surplus of £30,000 on income of £180,000 is 16.7%, which is better than a larger surplus of £32,000 on £220,000, which is 14.5%. A mean of several figures is the total divided by the number of values: quarterly sales of £120k, £150k, £135k and £165k total £570k, so the mean is £142.5k. The median is the middle value after sorting, or the average of the middle two. Pie charts use angles of a full 360 degrees: 144 degrees is 144/360 = 40% of the total. Cost per head divides total cost by the number of staff. Percentage growth compares the change with the earlier figure. Be careful to use the right base and the right period. If answers differ only in the unit, such as thousands or millions, check the unit in the question.

questions.prompt: Income and spending were: 2021 income £180k, spend £150k; 2022 income £200k, spend £170k; 2023 income £220k, spend £188k. In which year was the surplus the largest share of income?

options.text: 2023, because it had the largest income

questions.prompt: Quarterly sales were £120k, £150k, £135k and £165k. What was the mean sales figure per quarter?
A department has 600 staff. 35% are in Grade A, 45% in Grade B and the rest in Grade C. How many staff are in Grade C?
Cases closed in five weeks were 24, 30, 27, 33 and 31. What is the difference between the median and the mean?
questions.hint: Mean = 145 ÷ 5 = 29; median = 30; difference 1.

questions.prompt: A pie chart shows housing as a sector of 144 degrees. The total budget is £7.5 million. How much is spent on housing?

options.text: £3 million
£1.5 million
£4.5 million
£0.4 million

questions.prompt: Department A has 45 staff and a pay bill of £2.25 million. Department B has 60 staff and a pay bill of £2.7 million. Which has the lower pay cost per head, and by how much?

options.text: Department B, by £5,000
Department A, by £5,000
Department B, by £0.45 million
Department A, by £50,000

questions.hint: A: £50,000 per head; B: £45,000 per head; B is lower by £5,000.

questions.prompt: Visits were 20,000 in 2021, 24,000 in 2022 and 27,600 in 2023. What was the percentage growth from 2022 to 2023?
Site A passed 54 of 72 candidates and Site B passed 45 of 50. Which site has the higher pass rate, and by how many percentage points?

options.text: Site A, by 15 percentage points
Site B, by 20 percentage points
Site B, by 15 percentage points
Site A, because it passed more people

questions.hint: A: 54/72 = 75%; B: 45/50 = 90%; the difference is 15 points.

items.title: Numerical reasoning: units, scale, time zones and rates (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: The hardest practical questions combine unit conversion with rates. Plan the order: convert everything to the same unit first, then calculate. A journey from 08:50 to 11:05 is 2 hours 15 minutes, which is 2.25 hours, so at 96 km/h the distance is 216 km. Never use 2.15 for 2 hours 15 minutes. For cutting or packing, divide and round down to whole pieces: 2.4 m is 240 cm, and 240 ÷ 35 = 6.86, so 6 whole pieces. For volume, 1 cubic metre holds 1,000 litres, so 1.5 cubic metres is 1,500 litres, and at 20 litres a minute it empties in 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes. A model scale of 1:50 means the real object is 50 times larger, so a 6.5 m height is 650 cm real, and 13 cm on the model. Time zones add or subtract hours after you have found the travel time: a 3 hour 20 minute flight leaving at 09:40 lands at 13:00 by departure time, and at 14:00 local time if the destination is one hour ahead. For combined machines, add their rates. Fuel use per 100 km multiplies by the distance in hundreds of km. Finally, check the answer's unit.

questions.prompt: A train travels from 08:50 to 11:05 at an average speed of 96 km/h. How far does it travel?

options.text: 192 km
240 km
288 km
216 km

questions.hint: The time is 2.25 hours; 96 × 2.25 = 216 km.

questions.prompt: A 2.4 m length of ribbon is cut into pieces that are each 35 cm long. How many whole pieces can be cut?
questions.hint: 2.4 m = 240 cm; 240 ÷ 35 = 6.86, so 6 whole pieces.

questions.prompt: A tank holds 1.5 cubic metres of water and empties at 20 litres a minute. How long does it take to empty? (1 cubic metre = 1,000 litres)

options.text: 1 hour 5 minutes
1 hour 30 minutes
1 hour 15 minutes
2 hours 15 minutes

questions.hint: 1,500 ÷ 20 = 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes.

questions.prompt: A scale model is built at 1:50. The real building is 6.5 m high. How high is the model?

options.text: 650 cm
130 cm
1.3 cm
13 cm

questions.prompt: A flight leaves at 09:40 UK time and lasts 3 hours 20 minutes. The destination is one hour ahead of UK time. What is the local arrival time?
questions.hint: 09:40 + 3:20 = 13:00 UK time; add 1 hour for local time = 14:00.

questions.prompt: Machine A makes 40 items an hour and Machine B makes 60 items an hour. They run together for 3 hours. How long would Machine B alone take to make the same number?

options.text: 7.5 hours
3 hours
5 hours
4.5 hours

questions.hint: Together they make 100 × 3 = 300 items; 300 ÷ 60 = 5 hours.

questions.prompt: An annual bill of £1,860 is paid in 10 equal monthly instalments, and each instalment has a £2.50 fee. How much is each payment?
A car uses 8.4 litres of fuel per 100 km. Fuel costs £1.50 a litre. What is the fuel cost of a 350 km trip?

items.title: Verbal reasoning: true, false or cannot say, reports with figures (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: At the highest level the passages are longer and denser, and the statements may be built from combinations of facts. The method is unchanged but you must be more systematic. First, read the passage and mark every number, name and qualifier. Second, translate each sentence into a short note. Third, take the statement and break it into parts. Every part must be supported for the answer to be True, and one contradicted part makes it False. If all parts are consistent but one part is not covered, it is Cannot say. Be alert for statements that look like reasonable inferences but go further than the text: that a trend will continue, that something caused something else, or that a share of a total means the same as a share of a part. For example, if the passage says '30% of the 400 staff surveyed work part-time', then 120 surveyed staff work part-time, but that tells you nothing about all staff in the organisation. If the passage says 'the majority', then more than half. If it says 'a significant minority', the passage has not given a figure. Take care over time words such as 'since', 'by the end of' and 'in the previous year'. Reread before you finalise.

questions.prompt: "A survey of 400 civil servants found that 30% work part-time. Of those who work part-time, two thirds said they were satisfied with their working pattern. The survey was carried out in one department." Statement: "80 of the part-time staff surveyed said they were satisfied with their working pattern." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: two thirds of 400 is about 267
Cannot say: the survey covers only one department
Cannot say: the passage does not say which working pattern is used
True: 30% of 400 is 120, and two thirds of 120 is 80

questions.prompt: "The agency reduced the average time to process a claim from 21 days to 14 days. It credits a new triage process. An independent review is due to report next year." Statement: "The independent review has already confirmed that the triage process reduced processing times." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: the agency credits the new process
False: the review is not due to report until next year
Cannot say: the passage does not give the total number of claims handled
Cannot say: the passage does not say what triage is

questions.hint: The agency credits the process, but the independent review has not yet reported, so it is not proved.

questions.prompt: "Spending on training rose by 8% last year, reaching £4.5 million. Over the same period the number of staff grew by 12%. The department says it intends to raise training spending again." Statement: "Spending on training per member of staff fell last year." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: spending on training rose last year
Cannot say: the number of staff is not given
True: spending grew by less than the number of staff
Cannot say: the passage does not say what the department's plans are

questions.hint: Total spend grew 8% while staff grew 12%, so spend per head fell.

questions.prompt: "The report notes that most complaints about the helpline concerned long waiting times. A significant minority concerned the attitude of advisers. Very few complaints were about the accuracy of advice." Statement: "More than a quarter of complaints concerned the attitude of advisers." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: Cannot say: 'a significant minority' is not a figure
True: it was a significant minority
False: only a few complaints concerned attitude
False: most of the complaints concerned the attitude of advisers

questions.hint: The passage gives no number for the minority, so a quarter cannot be confirmed.

questions.prompt: "The pilot scheme ran in five regions between January and June. Applications were processed 25% faster in the pilot regions than elsewhere. The scheme will now be extended to all regions by the end of the year." Statement: "The scheme will operate in every region by the end of the year." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: it has only been tested in five regions
Cannot say: the passage does not name the regions
True: it will be extended to all regions by year end
Cannot say: the passage does not say whether the scheme was successful

questions.hint: The final sentence states the planned extension to all regions.

questions.prompt: "The charity received 2,000 donations in March, of which 1,500 were under £20. The average donation was £35. The charity says that it relies on a small number of large gifts." Statement: "Most donations in March were under £20." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: the average donation was £35
True: 1,500 out of 2,000 is 75%
Cannot say: the largest gift is not given
Cannot say: the charity's total income is not given

questions.hint: 1,500 of 2,000 is three quarters, so most donations were under £20.

questions.prompt: "Staff turnover in the department was 12% last year, compared with 9% the year before. The department introduced exit interviews in the second half of last year. It plans to publish the findings next spring." Statement: "Exit interviews are the reason that staff turnover rose last year." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: turnover rose in the year exit interviews began
False: exit interviews were introduced before the year began
Cannot say: the passage gives no reason for the rise in turnover
False: staff turnover did not rise last year

questions.hint: The passage reports the rise and the interviews, but does not link them.

questions.prompt: "Applications for the apprenticeship scheme closed on 31 October. Candidates who pass the online test will be invited to an assessment day. Assessment days will take place during November." Statement: "Every candidate who applied will be invited to an assessment day in November." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: assessment days take place in November
Cannot say: the passage does not say how many assessment days there will be
Cannot say: the date of the online test is not given
False: only candidates who pass the online test will be invited

questions.hint: Only those who pass the online test are invited.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: true, false or cannot say, policy and law-style passages (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Passages about regulations, entitlements and procedures are written in a precise style, with long sentences and conditions. The key is to break the rule into parts: who it applies to, what must be done, by when, and what the exceptions are. Words such as 'shall', 'must' and 'is required to' mean obligation. 'May' means permission. 'Provided that', 'subject to' and 'unless' introduce conditions. Worked example: 'A claimant shall be notified of a decision within 28 days of the claim being received, provided that all required documents have been supplied.' The statement 'A claimant who supplied all documents must be notified within 28 days' is True. The statement 'A claimant who supplied no documents must still be notified within 28 days' is False, because the condition has not been met. The statement 'The decision will be in the claimant's favour' is Cannot say. Be careful with counting days, such as 'within 28 days of receipt', which starts from when the claim is received and not from when it is sent. Where there are several conditions joined by 'and', all must be met; where they are joined by 'or', one is enough. Finally, make sure you answer about the specific person in the statement.

questions.prompt: "A claimant shall be notified of a decision within 28 days of the claim being received, provided that all required documents have been supplied." Statement: "A claimant who has supplied all the required documents must be notified within 28 days of receipt." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: notification takes longer than 28 days
True: the notification duty applies when documents are supplied
Cannot say: the passage does not say what the documents are
Cannot say: the passage does not say how a claimant is notified

questions.hint: All documents supplied means the 28-day rule applies.

questions.prompt: "Staff who work more than six hours must take a break of at least 20 minutes. Staff under 18 must take a 30-minute break once they have worked four and a half hours." Statement: "A 17-year-old who has worked four and a half hours must take a 30-minute break." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: breaks are only required after six hours
Cannot say: the passage does not say when the break is taken
True: the rule for staff under 18 applies at that point
Cannot say: the passage does not give the length of the shift

questions.hint: The under-18 rule covers a 17-year-old after four and a half hours.

questions.prompt: "Employees who have worked for the department for at least six months, or who have a written agreement from their manager, may apply to work flexibly. Applications must be answered within one month." Statement: "An employee with four months' service and no written agreement may apply to work flexibly." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: employees may apply to work flexibly
False: neither condition for applying is met
Cannot say: the passage does not say how to apply
Cannot say: the passage does not say what flexible working is

questions.hint: Either six months' service or a written agreement is needed, and the employee has neither.

questions.prompt: "Grants of up to £10,000 are available to community groups registered as charities. Groups must provide accounts for the last two years, unless they were formed in the last 12 months." Statement: "A charity formed eight months ago must provide two years of accounts." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: groups formed in the last 12 months are exempt
True: groups must provide two years of accounts
Cannot say: the passage does not say how to submit accounts
Cannot say: the passage does not say how many grants there are

questions.hint: The 'unless' clause exempts a group that is only eight months old.

questions.prompt: "Expenses must be claimed within three months of the date on which they were incurred. Claims made after that date will be paid only if the manager of the claimant approves a late submission." Statement: "A claim made after four months will be paid if the manager approves it." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: late claims are paid if a manager approves them
False: claims after three months are never paid
Cannot say: the passage does not say how much the claim is
Cannot say: the passage does not say which manager approves

questions.hint: The passage allows late claims with manager approval.

questions.prompt: "Visitors to the secure area must be escorted at all times. Contractors with a green pass need not be escorted but must sign in at the guardroom." Statement: "A contractor with a green pass must be escorted in the secure area." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: visitors must be escorted at all times
False: green pass holders need not be escorted
Cannot say: the passage does not say what a green pass is
Cannot say: the passage does not say where the guardroom is

questions.hint: Contractors with green passes are exempted from escorts.

questions.prompt: "The regulations require that complaints be acknowledged within five working days. A full response must follow within 30 working days, or the complainant must be told the reason for any delay." Statement: "A complainant must be told the reason if a full response takes longer than 30 working days." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: the response must always come within 30 days
True: the regulations require the reason for any delay
Cannot say: the passage does not say who the complainant is
Cannot say: the passage does not say how a delay is explained

questions.hint: The rule says that either the response arrives in 30 days or a reason is given.

questions.prompt: "Applicants must be over 18 and must hold either a full driving licence or a valid bus pass. Priority is given to people who live in the borough." Statement: "An applicant aged 17 with a bus pass meets the requirements." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: a valid bus pass is enough
Cannot say: the passage does not say where the applicant lives
False: applicants must be over 18
Cannot say: the passage does not define a bus pass

questions.hint: The age requirement is not met.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: strongest inference from several facts (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Some of the hardest verbal questions give you a group of connected facts and ask which statement must be true, or is most strongly supported. You need to hold several facts at once. Start by listing what the passage says about each person, group or item. Combine facts that are about the same thing. Then test each option. A 'must be true' option has to follow whatever else might be the case. An option that is merely possible, likely or sensible is not correct. Consider this set: 'All of the staff in the data team can use the system. Some staff in the data team are part-time. Nobody in the finance team is in the data team.' Then 'Some part-time staff can use the system' must be true, because the part-time staff in the data team are system users. 'No one in the finance team can use the system' does not follow, because they might be trained separately. Also be careful about the direction of statements and overlaps. Draw circles if it helps. If a question asks for the 'most strongly supported' option, it is allowed to be less than certain, but it must be the best-supported choice. Eliminate options that conflict with a fact first.

questions.prompt: All of the staff in the data team can use the system. Some staff in the data team are part-time. Nobody in the finance team is in the data team. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Some part-time staff can use the system
Nobody in the finance team can use the system
All part-time staff can use the system
Some finance team staff are part-time

questions.hint: The part-time staff who are in the data team can use the system.

questions.prompt: Every report in the archive is dated. No confidential report may be copied. The Q3 report is in the archive and is confidential. Which statement must be true?

options.text: The Q3 report is dated but may be copied if a manager agrees
The Q3 report is dated and may not be copied
All dated reports in the archive may not be copied
Every report in the archive is confidential

questions.hint: The Q3 report is archived, so it is dated, and it is confidential, so it may not be copied.

questions.prompt: Maya works fewer hours than Noel. Noel works fewer hours than Omar. Omar works the same hours as Priya. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Maya works more hours than Priya
Noel works more hours than Priya
Maya and Noel work the same hours
Priya works more hours than Maya

questions.hint: The order is Maya < Noel < Omar = Priya.

questions.prompt: Teams that use the new process complete cases faster. Team Red completes cases faster than Team Blue. Team Blue uses the new process. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Team Red uses the new process
Team Red may or may not use the new process
Team Red does not use the new process
Team Blue completes more cases than Team Red

questions.hint: Using the process is one reason for speed; Red could be faster for other reasons.

questions.prompt: Of the 60 staff in an office, 45 have attended safety training. Of the 15 who have not, 10 are new starters. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Ten staff who have attended the training are also new starters
All new starters have not attended training
Forty-five staff who attended training are not new starters at all
Five staff who have not attended training are not new starters

questions.hint: 15 − 10 = 5 staff who have not attended training are not new starters.

questions.prompt: Visitors can park in Zone A only after 5pm. The staff car park is Zone B. Zone C is for disabled drivers at all times. Sam is a visitor who parked in Zone A and followed the rules. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Sam parked before 5pm
Sam parked in the staff car park
Sam parked after 5pm
Sam is a disabled driver

questions.hint: Visitors may use Zone A only after 5pm, so Sam parked after 5pm.

questions.prompt: Only people with a level 3 clearance can read file X. Tara can read file X. Ben has a level 2 clearance. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Tara has level 3 clearance and Ben cannot read file X
Ben can read file X if a manager gives special approval to him
Tara and Ben have the same clearance
Tara has level 2 clearance

questions.hint: The 'only' rule means readers hold level 3, so a level 2 holder cannot read it.

questions.prompt: In a survey, more staff chose option A than option B. Fewer staff chose option C than option B. Option D was chosen by as many staff as option A. Which option was chosen by the fewest staff?

options.text: Option B
Option A
Option D
Option C

questions.hint: The order is A = D > B > C.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: spotting flaws and weak reasoning (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: At level 5 you may be asked to judge the quality of an argument. Typical flaws include confusing correlation with cause, generalising from a small or unusual sample, assuming that what is true of the whole is true of each part, and relying on an authority who has an interest in the outcome. Take the claim: 'Staff who use the gym are more productive, so the gym makes staff more productive.' The flaw is that more productive people may be more likely to use the gym, or both may depend on a third factor such as good health. A survey of ten volunteers cannot show what is true of 10,000 staff. A claim that 'the department saved money because it cut spending' is circular. To spot the flaw, find the conclusion and the evidence. Then ask what else could explain the evidence, and how typical the evidence is. In a test, you will usually be asked which statement describes the weakness, or which fact would most weaken the argument. Choose the option that names the real gap in the reasoning, not one that merely disagrees with the conclusion or introduces an unrelated fact. Keep your answer linked to the passage.

questions.prompt: Staff who use the on-site gym are more productive, so the gym makes staff more productive. What is the main weakness in this argument?

options.text: The gym may be too small for all staff
Productivity is hard to measure in every office
Some staff prefer to exercise outside work
More productive or healthier staff may be the ones who choose to use the gym

questions.hint: The argument treats a link as proof that the gym causes the productivity.

questions.prompt: A manager asked five team members whether the new rota is fair. All five said yes, so she concluded that all 300 staff think the rota is fair. What is the main weakness?

options.text: Staff may not fully understand how the new rota will work
The manager should have asked only the managers in the team instead
The sample of five is too small and may not represent all staff
Rotas should never be changed once they have been set

questions.hint: A small group cannot show what 300 people think.

questions.prompt: The department's director says the new process is excellent. The director designed the process. What is the main weakness in using this as evidence?

options.text: The director has an interest in the process being seen as a success
The director may be too busy to check
The process may be expensive
The department may have several directors

questions.hint: A person with a personal interest is not a neutral source.

questions.prompt: Complaints about the service fell last month, so the new training course has worked. Which fact would most weaken this conclusion?

options.text: The course lasted three days
Staff liked the trainer
The course was held in London
The helpline was closed for part of the month, so fewer people could complain

questions.hint: Fewer complaints may be due to the closure, not to the training.

questions.prompt: A town with a new cycle lane has seen a fall in car journeys of 10%. The council claims the lane caused the fall. Which fact would most strengthen the claim?

options.text: Surveys show many former drivers now say that they use the cycle lane instead
The cycle lane is painted green
The council built the lane in the spring
The town is in the south of England

questions.hint: Drivers switching to the lane directly supports the claim.

questions.prompt: Because the organisation is made up of many highly skilled individuals, it must be a highly effective organisation. What is the main weakness?

options.text: It assumes the organisation is large
It assumes that what is true of the parts must be true of the whole
It does not say what the skills are
It ignores salary levels

questions.hint: Skilled members do not guarantee that the organisation works well together.

questions.prompt: A report says that areas with more police have more crime, and so police cause crime. What is the most likely flaw?

options.text: Police numbers are difficult to count accurately in every area
Crime is reported differently in each area and in each year
Some areas have more roads
Police may be sent to areas that already have more crime

questions.hint: The cause may run the other way: crime attracts police.

questions.prompt: A survey of customers who completed an online feedback form found that 90% were satisfied. The department concluded that 90% of all customers are satisfied. Which weakness is most serious?

options.text: Customers who complete a form may not represent those who do not
The form may have had too many questions for most customers to answer
The survey took place online rather than by telephone or post
Satisfaction is a vague idea that is difficult to put into numbers

questions.hint: Only those who chose to respond are included, which can bias the result.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: purpose, tone and implication (level 5)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: The last type of verbal question asks about the writer's purpose, tone or what is implied rather than stated. The purpose could be to inform, to persuade, to warn, to explain or to reassure. The tone could be neutral, cautious, critical or encouraging. An implication is something the passage suggests without saying it directly. Start by asking, 'Why was this written, and for whom?' A notice that says 'Staff are reminded that tailgating through the entrance is a breach of security policy' is a warning or reminder, with a firm tone. Look at word choices. Words such as 'unfortunately', 'concern' and 'failed' are negative. Words such as 'encouraging', 'welcome' and 'improved' are positive. Hedging words such as 'may', 'appears' and 'suggests' show caution. An implication must be a reasonable reading of the text, not a guess. If a passage says 'The service has not met its targets for three years running', the implication is that the service has repeatedly underperformed. It does not imply that managers are to blame. Stay close to the text, and avoid options that make a dramatic leap.

questions.prompt: Staff are reminded that tailgating through the entrance is a breach of security policy and may result in disciplinary action. What is the main purpose of this notice?

options.text: To invite staff to suggest changes to the entrance and security rules
To announce that the entrance is being rebuilt
To warn staff about a security rule and its consequences
To thank staff for their recent efforts

questions.hint: The notice reminds staff of a rule and warns of consequences.

questions.prompt: The service has not met its targets for three years running. Which implication is best supported?

options.text: The service is about to close
The managers have been replaced
The service has repeatedly underperformed
The targets that were set for the service were unrealistic

questions.hint: Failing for three years running implies repeated underperformance.

questions.prompt: The early results are encouraging, although it is too soon to draw firm conclusions. What is the tone of this statement?

options.text: Strongly critical
Completely neutral
Dismissive
Cautiously positive

questions.hint: 'Encouraging' is positive, and 'too soon' adds caution.

questions.prompt: Unfortunately, the survey response rate was only 18%, which limits what can be said about staff views. What does the writer imply?

options.text: The staff have no opinion
The survey will be repeated again next week to check
The results should be treated with caution
The survey was well designed

questions.hint: A low response rate means the results may not represent all staff.

questions.prompt: The minister welcomed the report and said she would study its recommendations carefully before responding. What does this suggest about the minister's position?

options.text: She has rejected the recommendations
She has already put all of the report's recommendations into action
She has not yet decided whether to accept the recommendations
She did not read the report

questions.hint: Studying the recommendations before responding means no decision yet.

questions.prompt: This guidance explains how to complete the form in four steps. It uses simple language and gives an example for each step. Who is the guidance mainly written for?

options.text: Experts in tax law
People who are completing the form for the first time
Inspectors who check forms
Managers who design forms

questions.hint: Simple language and examples suggest it is for beginners.

questions.prompt: While the new system has reduced paperwork, a number of staff have reported difficulty in using it. The department is therefore reviewing its training. What is the main point?

options.text: The system should be withdrawn
The training was a success
Staff do not want to use computers
The system has benefits, but problems with its use are being addressed

questions.hint: The passage balances a benefit with a problem and a response.

questions.prompt: It is hoped that the changes will ease pressure on the service, but their effect will not be known until next year. What does the writer imply about the changes?

options.text: They have already worked well in every part of the service
Their success is uncertain at present
They will be cancelled
They are unpopular

questions.hint: 'Hoped' and 'not known until next year' suggest uncertainty.

items.title: Situational judgement: integrity under pressure (level 5)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Level 5 situational judgement questions put real pressure on your integrity. There may be a deadline, a senior person pushing you, or a friendly colleague asking a favour. Several options can look defensible, so test each against the Civil Service Code: honesty, integrity, objectivity and impartiality. The strongest answers refuse to compromise on honesty or the rules but remain constructive, offering a legitimate way forward and involving the right person. Weak answers give in to pressure, take a shortcut, hide information or ignore the problem. The best answer is not always the most dramatic one. Escalating a small problem to the top, or confronting someone publicly, can be as poor as saying nothing. Think about proportion. Worked example: your director asks you to adjust a figure in a performance report so that a target looks met. The best response is to explain that you cannot change the figure because the report must be accurate, offer to explain the result or add context, and raise your concern with a senior manager or the proper channel if the pressure continues. Avoid answers that comply quietly or that refuse without suggesting an alternative.

questions.prompt: Your director asks you to adjust a figure in a performance report so a target looks met. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Explain that the report must be accurate, offer to add context, and raise concerns with a senior manager if pressed
Change the figure, as the director is more senior and may know more
Change the figure slightly so that the difference is small and unlikely to be noticed
Refuse and tell the whole team what the director has asked you to do

questions.hint: Accuracy is non-negotiable, but you can help by explaining the result honestly.

questions.prompt: A close friend in your team asks you to approve their expenses without the receipts, saying they lost them. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Explain that receipts are required, suggest they ask for duplicates and offer to help them follow the process
Approve it this time but tell them it must not happen again
Approve it after asking them to write a note that the receipts were lost
Refuse and report them to your manager without speaking to them

questions.hint: Treating a friend the same as anyone else, while helping them find a proper route, is fair and constructive.

questions.prompt: You are told to meet a target by Friday, and you realise the only way is to skip a required check on a set of applications. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Skip the check for the applications that look straightforward and low risk
Skip the check, as the target is a priority
Complete the checks later but record that they were all done earlier
Tell your manager the check cannot be skipped and discuss the deadline

questions.hint: The check protects the public, so the target must be discussed rather than the check skipped.

questions.prompt: A minister's adviser asks you for figures that you know show a policy in a poor light, asking you to leave out the worst numbers. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Leave out the worst numbers as asked
Give the adviser the figures but mark them as draft to delay their use for as long as possible
Explain you must give accurate information and tell your manager about the request
Send the full figures to the press

questions.hint: Civil servants provide honest and objective information, and your manager should know of the request.

questions.prompt: You discover that a colleague has been copying their own work from an old report and presenting it as new analysis. The decision-makers rely on it. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Rewrite the analysis yourself without telling anyone
Ignore it, as the colleague is experienced
Tell the decision-makers directly that the colleague is unreliable and cannot be trusted
Raise your concern with your manager, setting out what you have seen

questions.hint: Raising it with your manager lets the right person check the work fairly.

questions.prompt: You are offered a job by a company that has just won a contract you helped to evaluate. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Accept the offer and tell your manager when you resign
Tell your manager about the offer straight away and ask for advice
Keep the offer quiet until the contract has properly started and then accept it
Decline without telling anyone

questions.hint: Disclosure protects the integrity of the earlier decision.

questions.prompt: A senior colleague tells you that the department's rules are too strict and suggests you bend them in a small way to help a customer. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Bend the rules, because the customer will benefit
Bend the rules but keep a note for yourself
Explain that you need to follow the rules and offer to find another way of helping the customer
Ask the customer to complain so the rules can be reviewed

questions.hint: Rules should be followed, and you can still look for legitimate help.

questions.prompt: You realise a decision you made last week was based on a calculation you now think was wrong. It benefited a customer. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Say nothing, since the customer has benefited
Change the record so it matches the correct calculation without telling anyone
Contact the customer and ask them to return the money
Check the calculation and tell your manager if it was wrong

questions.hint: Reporting the possible error lets the department decide how to put it right.

items.title: Situational judgement: vulnerable customers and safeguarding (level 5)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Some customers are vulnerable, for example because of age, illness, disability, bereavement or financial hardship. Situational judgement questions test how you recognise this and respond with care while keeping to the rules. Look for signs such as confusion, distress, difficulty reading letters, or comments suggesting a risk to themselves or others. Effective responses are patient, use plain language, check understanding, and offer extra support or adjustments, such as a longer call or a different format. Where there is a risk to safety, follow your safeguarding procedure and speak to your manager straight away. Do not promise to keep a safety concern secret. At the same time, do not share personal information more widely than you must. Worked example: an elderly customer rings in some distress, repeating that she cannot manage her bills and has nobody to help. A strong response is to listen, take your time, explain the help available, offer to arrange support, and follow your procedures if there are signs of risk. A poor response is to rush the call, refer her to the website, or hand over her details to a third party who has not been verified.

questions.prompt: An elderly customer rings in distress, saying she cannot manage her bills and has no one to help. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Listen patiently, explain the help available and follow the procedure for vulnerable customers
Refer her to the website and end the call as quickly as possible
Offer to speak to her neighbour and explain her bills to them
Tell her that bills are the customer's own responsibility

questions.hint: Patient, practical help and following the procedure is the right response.

questions.prompt: A customer tells you during a call that their partner controls all of their money and they are frightened to go home. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Tell them to speak to their partner about the problem
Take it seriously, stay calm, follow the safeguarding procedure and speak to your manager immediately
Promise to keep it entirely secret and not tell anyone
Suggest they ring back when they feel less upset

questions.hint: There is a risk to safety, so the safeguarding process must be followed.

questions.prompt: A customer who cannot read well asks you to explain a letter, and says they are embarrassed. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Tell them to ask a family member to read it
Reassure them, explain the letter clearly and offer to send information in an easier format
Read the letter out quickly and finish the call
Suggest they should learn to read better

questions.hint: Respecting their dignity and offering adjustments is the best response.

questions.prompt: A caller says they are phoning on behalf of their elderly father and wants details of his claim. You cannot verify their authority. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Explain that you need the father's consent and describe how it can be given
Give the details, since the caller sounds genuine
Give only the amount of his claim
Refuse to speak to the caller at all

questions.hint: Personal data may only be shared with consent, but you can explain the route.

questions.prompt: A customer mentions that they have not eaten for two days because their payment is delayed. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Check what emergency help is available and arrange it under the procedure, then explain the next steps
Tell them the payment will arrive soon
Suggest they try a food bank without checking any support
Say you can do nothing until the payment date

questions.hint: Hardship needs a prompt, procedural response and honest information.

questions.prompt: A customer with a hearing impairment struggles on the phone. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Raise your voice and repeat everything
Ask them to bring a friend to the office
Offer to use another way of communicating, such as text or letter, and record their preference
Tell them they must use the phone for security

questions.hint: Reasonable adjustments allow equal access to the service.

questions.prompt: During a call, a customer says they are overwhelmed and no longer want to continue living. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Tell them that things will improve soon and end the call politely
Give them the number for a general advice service and hang up
Stay on the line, show care, follow the emergency procedure and alert your manager at once
Say you are not trained and transfer the call without any explanation to the caller

questions.hint: This is an immediate risk, and following the emergency process is the priority.

questions.prompt: A frequent caller is often confused and repeats the same question. Other customers are waiting. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Stay patient, answer clearly, note the pattern and ask your manager about extra support
Tell them they have already been given the answer
End the call quickly to help the others
Ignore their calls in future

questions.hint: Patience and referring for extra support helps the customer and the service.

items.title: Situational judgement: leading by example and handling change (level 5)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Even in entry-level roles, civil servants are expected to show leadership behaviours: setting a good example, supporting others, being resilient and helping the team to adapt. Situational judgement questions at this level ask you to act when there is no clear instruction. Effective responses are proactive but within your remit. For instance, if a new colleague seems lost, you offer help. If a process is not working, you collect evidence and suggest an improvement to the right person. If the team is under strain, you stay positive and practical. You should avoid taking over, acting beyond your authority, or complaining without offering solutions. Worked example: a major change is announced and your colleagues are anxious and complaining. A strong response is to listen, share accurate information, avoid gossip, ask your manager to answer the team's questions, and focus on what you can influence. A weak response is to join in the complaining or to ignore your colleagues. When a colleague has behaved badly, you can address it calmly in private. Remember that you are judged on your own conduct, and your actions influence how others behave.

questions.prompt: A major change is announced and your colleagues are anxious and complaining. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Listen, share accurate information, avoid gossip and ask your manager to answer the team's questions
Join the complaints so that colleagues feel supported
Tell them to stop complaining and get on with it
Say nothing and keep your head down

questions.hint: Staying constructive and seeking answers helps the team adapt.

questions.prompt: A new colleague seems lost and is not asking for help. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Wait for them to ask you for help
Offer help kindly, show them where to find guidance and tell them whom to ask
Tell your manager they are not coping
Do their work so they do not fall behind

questions.hint: A friendly offer of help supports them without taking over.

questions.prompt: Your team has been given a new target with fewer staff. Morale is low. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Tell your manager that the target is impossible
Suggest the team agrees priorities with the manager and raise realistic concerns with evidence
Work extra hours without telling anyone
Do only what you did before and ignore the target

questions.hint: Practical suggestions backed with evidence are more useful than complaint.

questions.prompt: You notice a process is causing delays every week. Nobody has raised it. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Collect examples and suggest a possible improvement to your manager
Wait for someone more senior to notice
Change the process for yourself without telling anyone else about the change
Complain about the process to colleagues

questions.hint: Evidence and a suggestion are constructive and within your remit.

questions.prompt: A colleague you work with closely has made a mistake that you spot before it goes out. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Point it out to them politely and help them to correct it
Fix it without saying anything
Tell your manager about the mistake before you tell the colleague at all
Let it go out and see what happens

questions.hint: Open, kind feedback fixes the issue and helps the colleague learn.

questions.prompt: You are asked to cover a task that is outside your usual role, and you have not been trained. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Refuse since it is not your job
Do it your own way without asking
Say you are willing, ask for guidance and check what is expected
Accept it but tell nobody at all that you do not know how to do it

questions.hint: Willingness plus honesty about your limits is the best mix.

questions.prompt: You made a good suggestion that your manager adopted, but a senior leader praises your colleague by mistake. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Quietly let your manager or the leader know the facts, without making a fuss
Say nothing and resent it
Correct the leader in front of everyone
Take credit in the next team email

questions.hint: A calm, factual correction is honest and avoids damaging relationships.

questions.prompt: The team is under strain after a colleague leaves unexpectedly. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Take over all the leaver's work yourself
Offer to share tasks, suggest the manager reviews priorities and stay positive
Tell colleagues who you think caused the colleague to leave the team so quickly
Wait for the manager to fix it

questions.hint: Practical support and communication help the team through the change.

items.title: Situational judgement: public trust, media and political impartiality (level 5)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Civil servants serve the government of the day, whatever its political party, and must be seen to do so impartially. They must also protect the trust of the public. Situational judgement questions at level 5 test what you do when your work meets politics or the media. The rules are straightforward. Do not share your political views while acting as a civil servant, and be careful about what you post online. Do not speak to journalists on behalf of the department unless you are authorised; pass enquiries to the press office. Do not leak confidential information. Do not misuse official information for private gain. If you disagree with a policy, you can raise your concern through the proper route but you must still carry out lawful instructions. Worked example: a journalist phones you and asks about a decision your team made. The most effective response is to say that you are not able to comment and that the press office will help, then let your manager know about the call. Giving an informal view, even a positive one, is risky. Choose answers that protect impartiality, confidentiality and trust.

questions.prompt: A journalist phones you and asks about a decision your team made. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Give a brief, off-the-record explanation to be helpful
Say the decision was a mistake but you cannot say more
Hang up and tell nobody
Say you cannot comment, refer them to the press office and tell your manager about the call

questions.hint: Only authorised people speak to the media on the department's behalf.

questions.prompt: You strongly disagree with a new government policy that your team has to implement. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Refuse to work on the policy
Raise your concern with your manager and continue to carry out the work
Post your opinion on social media to put public pressure on the government
Do the work slowly to show your disagreement

questions.hint: Civil servants may raise concerns but must serve the government of the day.

questions.prompt: At a party event, a friend invites you to join a campaign group supporting a political party. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Join the group and use a different name
Check the rules for your grade on political activity and politely decline if you must stay impartial
Join and mention your department on the sign-up form
Join and encourage colleagues to join too

questions.hint: The Code requires political impartiality, so check the rules before getting involved.

questions.prompt: You come across a draft report marked sensitive that contains information about a policy not yet announced. A friend asks you what is coming. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Hint at the general direction in confidence
Tell your friend only a small part
Tell the friend to read the news
Say you cannot discuss unannounced policy and keep the information to yourself

questions.hint: Unannounced policy is confidential, and sharing it could harm trust.

questions.prompt: A member of the public posts an inaccurate claim about your department on social media. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Reply from your personal account to correct them and name the department
Report it to your communications team and leave the official reply to them
Reply under a false name to defend the department and its staff
Ignore it and not tell anybody in the communications team about it

questions.hint: Authorised communications staff should respond to inaccuracies.

questions.prompt: An MP's office phones you and asks for information about a constituent's case that you are not authorised to give. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Provide the information, because MPs represent the public
Provide only the outcome of the case
Explain politely that you cannot share it and pass the request to your manager or the correspondence team
Ask the MP's staff to call back until they give up

questions.hint: Information must be released through the right channels with proper authority.

questions.prompt: A minister's special adviser asks you to produce a short note arguing for the party's election pledge. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Write the note, as the request comes from a minister's team
Write the note in your own time
Ask a colleague to write it for you
Explain that civil servants cannot do party political work and tell your manager about the request

questions.hint: Party political work is outside the role of a civil servant.

questions.prompt: You are leaving the Civil Service and a company asks you to share what you know about a forthcoming government contract. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Share only public information that you already know is available
Share it if they promise to keep it secret
Share it after you have left
Decline, remind them of your duty of confidentiality and tell your manager of the approach

questions.hint: Confidentiality continues after leaving, and the approach should be reported.
